name: Nikhil Sehgal
subject: Application: Policy Analyst, Trade Policy
paragraphs: I am applying for the position of Policy Analyst in IISD's trade policy team. I bring over four years of work on sustainability regulation in consulting, at a listed company and at the Global Reporting Initiative, and a particular interest in how European trade-related rules affect the countries and companies that export to Europe.

Your report The State of Border Carbon Adjustments 2026 finds that the design of these measures largely decides how unevenly their costs fall on trading partners. My client work looks at the same question from the side of the companies affected, and I would like to contribute to research that helps policymakers anticipate such effects.

At KarbonWise, I advise companies in cement, building materials, industrial goods, automotive components and food on the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and the EU Deforestation Regulation. I assess what each measure requires of them and what it is likely to cost, and present the findings to management in written briefs; for one client this led to a compliance roadmap it then put into practice. At the Global Reporting Initiative in New Delhi, I assessed how EU measures affect companies in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. I have also analysed the EU-India free trade talks, the EU's Generalised Scheme of Preferences and the sustainability chapters of EU trade agreements.

At the Global Reporting Initiative I also evaluated how 53 member organisations in five countries engaged with the Sustainable Development Goals, using criteria I designed. I chaired the consortium's regular meetings, wrote its newsletters and policy briefs, hosted a webinar, and presented the GRI Standards at the stock exchanges in Bombay, Colombo and Dhaka. At KarbonWise I also prepare deliverables for an EU-funded LIFE project with its consortium partners and direct a team of analysts on client work.

My master's degree in Building Sustainability from TU Berlin included environmental law and WTO and trade law, and my thesis combined survey design with regression analysis in Python. I use Python and AI tools in my research and data work.

I hold a valid German work and residence permit and can start immediately. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the team's work on trade and sustainable development.
